topics.topic: Whether an existing imported VPS room may be renamed before export as an exception to room immutability
questions: May the owner rename an existing room in the VPS Registry before export as a one-time migration exception, or must the room remain immutable and the migration use some other explicitly decided way to replace the prohibited name?
How can the owner correct an existing VPS room name when R0-10 says a room is never renamed or removed, and A16 imports the name the v1 instance gave it?

When a picked VPS project has a room name that breaks R0-96, may the owner rename that existing room before export despite R0-10, or must the project remain unchanged and therefore be excluded or imported with the prohibited name?

quotes: A room is created in a project and listed; it is never renamed or removed.

So the owner, before making the export on the VPS (R0-72), corrects
there every room name of the projects to be picked that breaks this rule
(owner, 2026-11-23, State 0 round-59 T1).
judgement.divergence: For an existing VPS room with a prohibited name, the correction obligation changes that name before export, while the immutability obligation leaves it unchanged; the owner and readers of the imported room observe which name arrives.
judgement.why: In the admissible history where a picked VPS project already contains a prohibited room name, changing that name as required by R0-96 necessarily renames an existing room and therefore violates R0-10.
options: Allow a one-time pre-export rename of existing VPS rooms, explicitly narrowing R0-10.
Keep R0-10 absolute and let the import mapping accept owner-supplied replacement room names, explicitly changing A16 and the statement that the import renames no room.
Keep both Registry and import from renaming rooms, leaving no way to perform the required pre-export correction.
consequences: The first option preserves the required neutral imported name but creates an explicit exception to room immutability.
The second option preserves source-room immutability but changes the import's accepted outcome and mapping obligations.
The third option makes the required correction impossible whenever a picked project already has a prohibited room name.

witness.initial: The Registry on the VPS contains a project with an existing room whose name identifies a person's condition, and the owner picks that project for the one-time import.
events: The owner reviews the picked project's room names before export.
The owner encounters the R0-96 obligation to correct the prohibited room name on the VPS.
The owner makes the export and uploads it for import.
outcomes: R0-96 requires the owner to change the existing room name before export, so the imported room carries the corrected name.
R0-10 requires the existing room never to be renamed, so it retains the prohibited name and the required correction cannot occur.
witness.observer: The owner and later readers of the imported room, including the agent, see whether the corrected or original name is present.
basis:
The only source is the Registry on the VPS, imported once. At the import the
owner picks any subset of its projects; the import accepts whatever the owner
picks then, and the choice recorded here binds nothing.

As in R0-68 and R0-90, this is a rule on the writer — the owner, and the agent
through Kernel — not a check of Registry: Registry cannot tell what a word
means, refuses no name for its content and searches no text for words; a
name that breaks the rule does reach the agent.

The owner makes the export of a source with a one-time migration script run on
that source's host.

The owner uploads the export file (R0-72) in the owner interface. Registry
   reads it as data (A19) and answers, without changing anything, each
   project the file holds with its id and status.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
State 2: decide required results and constraints, including necessary refusal precedence; carry test mechanisms, exact contracts and deployment procedures to their owners.
